what: This is a preferred share of Huntington Bancshares, the Ohio-based regional bank. Unlike the bank's ordinary shares, it pays a fixed dividend, ranks ahead of ordinary shares if the bank is wound up, and does not participate in growth.
customers: The bank serves Midwestern households and businesses; this security is bought by investors seeking a fixed income payment.
money: deposits, mortgages, car and equipment lending
corporate lending, treasury management and specialty finance
moat: The underlying bank's deposit franchise across Ohio and Michigan, which funds lending cheaply and generates the earnings that support this dividend.
risks: The dividend is not contractually guaranteed and can be suspended
It ranks behind every lender to the bank
The market price falls when long-term interest rates rise
A severe credit downturn would put the payment at risk
opportunities: A yield well above the bank's ordinary dividend
Paid before ordinary shareholders receive anything
The bank's net margin of 27% gives a comfortable margin of coverage
watch: Huntington's capital ratios and credit losses, and continued declaration of the dividend.
